_what: does tightening the PITCH gate improve the metrics camera elevation drives, and can the population still be served?
_rule: ADOPT the tightest gate whose corrected movement is >= 3.0pp lower than at 16 deg AND whose availability is >= 60% of identities with >= 4 in-gate photographs. Otherwise DROP and record it. Pre-registered NEXT-FOUR §2.3 on 2026-09-08, before the data.
_both_sides_gated: the bank's own spread is recomputed from bank pose at the SAME gate as the noise term (trap 1).
_served_sensitivity: served_corrected_at_baseline_pct vs served_corrected_at_this_gate_pct measures the SAME people both ways — the population the gate would actually serve, scored at 16 deg with all their photographs and at gate g with only the in-gate ones. It answers whether the gate helps the people it keeps, which the all-comers figure cannot. REPORTED, not the pre-registered rule.
_matched_sensitivity: matched_corrected_movement_pct recomputes the movement AND the noise on the identities that clear 2K photographs at EVERY gate, so a gate difference cannot be a difference between people. REPORTED, not the pre-registered rule.
_bracket: corrected_movement uses the LFW noise term (years apart: photographic noise PLUS real change). floor_* uses Multiface (one instant) and is reported BESIDE it, never instead.
suspect_rule: Multiface within-subject SD >= 0.9 x LFW within-identity SD, DERIVED from scale_deconvolution.json
_asymmetry_row_caveat: asymmetry is measured here at |yaw| <= 14, NOT at the 5 deg yaw gate symmetry actually ships behind. It is not a statement about the tier-2 symmetry reading.
